text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Serbian government has still not started paying out late wages to the striking health sector despite an agreement reached on Tuesday. The strike, now in the fourth week, continues.
- Greek national telecommunications company OTE said it would purchase a 20 percent stake in Telecom Srbija.
- Twelve opposition parties sign agreement on minimum election conditions. Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO), Serbian Radical Party (SRS) and Vojvodina coalition not joining.
- Zagreb is slowing down the return of Croatian Serb refugees, says Radivoje Rajkovic, the head of Yugoslav part of the joint Yugoslav-Croatian commission on implementation of the bilateral accord.
- French central bank puts joint stock French-Yugoslav bank under receivership and replaces general manager Miodrag Zecevic because of dubious transactions.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT will be privatised by the year 2,000, says director Zika Petrovic.
POLITIKA
- Serbian Commodities Reserve Agency issues two tranches of 25 million dinar short-term bonds to finance production of agriculture machinery.
- Yugoslavia and Bulgaria sign a customs cooperation agreement in Belgrade.
- Only parts of the Serbian oil industry NIS and Power company EPS will be privatised, said member of the Serbian government expert team Dragan Djuricin.

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic will remain the principal figure in the Socialist Party of Serbia, in Serbia and in Yugoslavia regardless of what function he will hold, said SPS spokesman Ivica Dacic.
BORBA
- Certain progress was made at ex-Yugoslavia succession talks in Brussels, says head of Yugoslav team Kosta Mihajlovic.

- Yugoslavia will attempt to meet all demands of the international war crimes tribunal in the shortest possible time and in line with its international committments, Yugoslav Justic minister Zoran Knezevic told head of the tribunal office in Belgrade.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF

- Veselin Sljivancanin, one of the indictees of the international war crimes tribunal, says there are no grounds for him to be tried in The Hague and that his actions in Vukovar had nothing to do with war crimes.
- Zeljko Raznatovic "Arkan" says he is not on a list of indicted war criminals in the Hague.
GRADJANIN
- Serb-Albanian talks on Kosovo are being held in Athens. Talks started in January in Munich under the auspices of the German Berthelsmann foundation.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslav parliament session to be held on June 26. No agenda announced but parliament expected to elect the new Yugoslav president.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- There is an conflict within the state leadership on Montenegro's position in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, said Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Issues raised by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright during her visit to Belgrade refer primarily to Serbia but concequences will also affect Montenegro, editorial.
- Montgenegrin opposition leader Novak Kilibarda invites president Momir Bulatovic to take part in a parliamentary debate on government reconstruction.

- Head of Podgorica security centre Goran Zugic said the police secured cigarette transports and the president was informed of this, dewnying Bulatovic's accusations that his service was extorting tax for cigarette smuggling. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
